references.text: The angel of the Lord continues to stand in Balaam's way, this time on an even narrower path between vineyards
The angel of the Lord first stands in Balaam's way with a drawn sword, as the beginning of this series of obstacles
Balaam's eyes are finally opened, and he sees the angel of the Lord who had stood in his way
The angel explains that he stood in the way because Balaam's path was wrong in the Lord's sight
From distress I called out to the Lord, and the Lord answered me and brought me into a wide place - a contrast to the narrow place with no exit
When you walk, your steps will not be hindered - a contrast to Balaam, who came to a place where there was no road to the right or to the left
The command not to turn aside to the right or to the left from the Lord's way - Balaam could literally not turn aside
Israel must not turn aside to the right or to the left from the Lord's commands - parallel to the physical image of being unable to turn
